chunks: And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAṭiyyah, who said:

Sulaymān ibn Khālid asked him, while I was with him, about a man who circumambulated the House in six circuits. So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “And how does he circumambulate six circuits?” He said: “He faced the Stone, said: ‘Allāhu Akbar,’ and counted one.” He said: “He performs one circuit.” Sulaymān said: “If that escaped him until he came to his family?” He said: “He instructs someone to perform tawaf on his behalf.”

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: his family, meaning he returned home
key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: the takbir uttered at the start of counting or tawaf
key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: around the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House
key_terms.يَطُوفُ عَنْهُ: to perform tawaf on his behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs only six rounds of tawaf and returns home before completing the seventh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who completed only six circuits of tawaf. The Imam عليه السلام clarifies how the count occurred, rules that one more circuit must be performed, and if the person has already returned home, he should appoint someone to perform it on his behalf.
